headline: Microsoft's lighter capex and Alphabet's $9B cash burn (worst day in six years) put the spenders on trial, while suppliers with orders (Quanta, Trane, Vertiv) keep beating.
regime: A risk-on bounce in the AI suppliers (semis ETF +1.7%, cooling +4.7%, memory +5.5%) sits on top of a month-long drawdown (semis -6.5%, neoclouds -18.1%, foundry equipment -17.2%). The 10-year yield is now 5.05% and crude $101.82 (+13.9% on the month), so the discount rate keeps capping multiples. The new signal is the buyers: Microsoft's capex fell short on delayed third-party capacity, Alphabet posted negative free cash flow for a second quarter, and software sold off again after ServiceNow and Fortinet beat. Suppliers with backlog are paid; anything exposed to hyperscaler or neocloud spending decisions is not.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Quanta beat Q3 revenue expectations and the stock soared (e7171357cf02)
Trane Q3 revenue +17.7%, full-year revenue guidance raised (b3020387a9a1, 0765dff5592e)
GE Vernova posted record backlog and raised cash guidance, and is buying Trench for $9bn (4bc5c4c91ce6, f8381a9a0963)
Against: GE Vernova keeps falling on good news and the grid segment is -1.7% on five days, VST -8.6% (4bc5c4c91ce6)
theses.change_note: +2: another contractor and an HVAC maker confirm demand, but the market is still not paying for beats in grid and power, so the gain is small.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Marvell is reportedly in late-stage talks to buy Lumentum, a bet that optics are scarce (901fadf664d1, 28f6af9539f4)
Microsoft commercial backlog at $677bn and Azure accelerating (fee8c573bdbf)
Against: Microsoft and Alphabet capex came in lighter and Samsung missed on profit, hitting INTC, AMD, AVGO, MU (aee72467f967)
Against: Microsoft cited delayed third-party capacity, which is a supply problem but also a spending delay (1b605a7cb225)
theses.change_note: -4: demand evidence is intact, but two hyperscalers spending less than expected is the first direct dent from the buyers.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CRWV, NBIS, IREN, APLD fell after Microsoft's capex missed on delayed third-party capacity (1b605a7cb225)
IREN raised $363M of equipment financing against its GPUs, so it is borrowing against hardware (a884a611a78f)
Segment is -18.1% on the month; Galaxy passed on a tenant for its 830 MW Helios site (c960ca216f64)
theses.change_note: +3: Microsoft pushing out third-party capacity hits neocloud revenue timing directly while they keep borrowing against GPUs.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Segment +5.5% on the day, MU +7.6% on five days, yet -15.7% on the month (digest segments)
MU is on the Zacks Rank #1 growth list (b0dbf40272d4)
SK Hynix's shortage warning is lifting memory-linked equipment names like Onto (54ac05250198)
Against: Samsung's profit miss and lighter hyperscaler capex weigh on memory (aee72467f967)
theses.change_note: The Samsung miss and the rebound offset each other; the segment is still down 16% on the month with the shortage call unchallenged.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Alphabet posted negative free cash flow of $9.07B, a second straight quarter of burn, and had its worst day in over six years (1f900bb0149d, 045d15df7e26)
Institutions sold Alphabet on a capex report that looked like a cash bonfire (90d80f5207a0)
META is -12.2% on five days; Google admits AI search earns less than regular search (eebeee3351e5)
Against: Microsoft rose on strong results and ORCL is +11.9% on five days (7c88ab25bbb8)
theses.change_note: +6: Alphabet's cash burn and the market's reaction are the test we flagged yesterday, and it failed; Microsoft's clean quarter keeps this from being uniform.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: 10-year at 5.05% and crude $101.82 (+13.9% on the month) (digest tape)
Semis ETF -6.5% on the month, Nasdaq -0.9%, while the S&P is +0.9% (digest tape)
Software 'crushed again' after beats from ServiceNow and Fortinet, a sign the market punishes anything priced for perfection (e060f51d5cf1)
theses.change_note: +3: the 10-year moved above 5% and good prints are being sold in software and grid.

compute.note: +2.5% today but -7.0% on the month; lighter hyperscaler capex caps it.

foundry_equipment.note: -17.2% on the month, TER -9.3% on five days; memory-linked metrology is the better corner.

memory_storage.note: Shortage call intact and the group is -15.7% on the month.

networking_optical.note: Lumentum deal talk is a takeover bid, not a fundamental signal; -11.0% on the month.

servers.note: Beats are not enough, and Super Micro still trades near $36.

power_nuclear.note: VST -8.6% on five days but contracts keep coming (NuScale-Doosan); own cash-flow producers.

grid_electrical.note: Quanta beat and GE Vernova buys Trench; the market is not paying yet, which helps entry prices.

cooling_thermal.note: Trane raised guidance and VRT is +14.5% on five days; less margin of safety after the run.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Microsoft's delayed third-party capacity and GPU-backed borrowing; -18.1% on the month.

hyperscalers.note: Alphabet cash burn and META -12.2% on five days; Microsoft is the exception.

ai_software.note: Up 5.8% on the month, but ServiceNow and Fortinet sold off on beats.

risks: More hyperscaler capex trims after Microsoft and Alphabet would hit the whole supplier chain despite strong supplier orders.
A 10-year yield above 5% with crude above $100 extends multiple compression in crowded AI names.
Neocloud financing stress could cancel or delay GPU, power and cooling orders.
Sell-the-news reactions (GE Vernova, ServiceNow) show strong prints can still lose money.
Amazon and Intel report after the close and could move the whole group.
watch: Amazon and Intel results after the close for capex direction.
Whether the Marvell-Lumentum deal is announced next week and how optics names react.
Eaton (Nov. 3) and Arista earnings for grid and networking demand.
Whether neocloud stocks hold their rebound after Microsoft's capacity delay.
